description: Convert AWG wire gauge to diameter (mm/in), cross-section area and copper resistance per km — or go backwards from a measured diameter to AWG.

faqs.a: American Wire Gauge is a logarithmic wire-size standard: larger AWG numbers mean thinner wire. Each 3-gauge step halves the cross-section area.

faqs.q: How is diameter computed from AWG?
faqs.a: With the standard formula d = 0.005 × 92^((36−n)/39) inches, then converted to millimetres. Cross-section follows from π·d²/4.

faqs.q: How is resistance per km computed?
faqs.a: From R = ρ·L/A with annealed copper resistivity ρ = 1.68×10⁻⁸ Ω·m at 20 °C. Real installations run slightly higher due to temperature and stranding.

howto: Choose AWG → specs or diameter → AWG.
Enter the AWG number (0–40) or the diameter in mm.
Read diameter, cross-section and copper resistance instantly.
Use the reverse mode to identify an unknown wire from a caliper measurement.
title: Wire Gauge (AWG) Converter
